back: A length of DNA at a locus on a chromosome that codes for a polypeptide (or functional RNA); the unit of inheritance.
An alternative form of a gene at the same locus, differing in base sequence.
The observable characteristics of an organism, from its genotype interacting with the environment.
Tyrosinase (melanin synthesis); recessive alleles cause albinism.
β-globin; Hbˢ allele (glutamic acid → valine at position 6) causes sickle cell anaemia.
Factor VIII (clotting); X-linked recessive alleles cause haemophilia A.
Huntingtin; expanded CAG repeat (dominant) causes Huntington's disease.
Codes for an enzyme making active gibberellin (GA₁); le le plants make little and are dwarf.
Base sequence → mRNA → amino acid sequence → protein shape and function → phenotype.
